questions.stem: In the small intestine, glucose is absorbed into the blood even when the glucose concentration is already higher in the blood than in the gut. Which process allows this?

options.text: Filtration, because blood pressure forces glucose across the membrane
Active transport, because energy is used to move glucose against the concentration gradient
Osmosis, because glucose dissolves in water
Diffusion, because glucose naturally moves into the blood

questions.explanation: When the concentration of glucose in the blood is already higher than in the gut, diffusion alone cannot absorb any more glucose. Active transport uses energy from ATP to move the remaining glucose against the gradient, ensuring none is wasted.
